receipt.public_excerpt: The best model was truthful on 58% of questions

evidence_items.explanation: The study tested GPT-3, GPT-Neo/J, GPT-2 and a T5-based model and found substantial false-answer rates. This supports recurring factual failures in several families, but does not cover every released model, personal accusations or the asserted cause.

receipt.public_excerpt: it “hallucinates” facts and makes reasoning errors

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI acknowledges factual and reasoning failures in GPT-4. The disclosure supports those components for this model, without establishing the universal scope or causal mechanism.

receipt.public_excerpt: struggle to self-correct their reasoning without external feedback.

evidence_items.explanation: Experiments involving GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and Llama-2 support limitations in the tested self-correction methods. They do not establish that absent checking causes every listed failure in every released transformer.

evidence_items.explanation: The study reports improved verification and arithmetic reasoning through a structured prompting procedure without external feedback. evidence_items.explanation: The report describes SearchGPT presenting box-office closure dates as festival dates in its launch demonstration. evidence_items.explanation: The report reproduces the court's account of ChatGPT generating false embezzlement accusations, while explaining why OpenAI nevertheless won the defamation case. This later ruling is context for the distinction between false personal accusations and actionable defamation, not an in-period outcome or evidence about every model.

unresolved_gaps: No exhaustive inventory and evaluation of every transformer LLM released by 2024-07-28 was established.
The evidence does not document every listed failure category for every model, particularly occasional false personal accusations.
The SearchGPT evidence concerns one demonstration and does not establish recurrence.
No retrieved intervention establishes inadequate checking as a contributing cause across every model and every listed failure category.
Verification studies test particular procedures and tasks; their differing results do not resolve a universal architectural explanation.
